title: Expounders of difficult passages (Dorshei Chamurot)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: They are mentioned in Berakhot 24a: they expounded the verse ‘And your life shall hang before you’ as referring to one who hangs his tefillin; and in Pesachim 54a they expounded: ‘Anah was of disqualified lineage’; and in Chullin 134b: ‘The shoulder corresponds to the arm.’ Related to this is what we find in Kiddushin 22b, that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai [supplied רי"בז] would expound this verse kemin ha-chomer (homiletically); and similarly Sotah 15b regarding R-G [contextually Gamliel]. We also find ‘expounders of reshumot’ in the Mekhilta, Beshalach, tractate Vayissa, chapter 1: ‘The expounders of reshumot [said; supplied אמו]: They found no words of Torah, which are likened to water’; and there: ‘He showed him words of Torah that are likened to wood.’ There, chapter 4, on the passage ‘And they gathered it’: that the manna was ‘in the sweat of your brow’; and there, chapter 5, on the passage ‘And the house of Israel called’: ‘They called its name manna.’ In the Sifrei, Masei, on the passage ‘And he was not his enemy,’ the expounders of reshumot said: Three testimonies are written in the passage, to teach you that capital cases require thirty.

notes.text: The Mekhilta quotation prints אמו, an unclear word here; the last quotation says capital cases require thirty. Both readings remain as transmitted rather than silently corrected.

The supplied אמו remains explicitly marked; the whole saved Beeri Edition Vayassa 1 scalar reads אמרו (said) and explains they-found-no-water as words of Torah likened to water. The English uses that contextual speech verb while keeping Hyman’s compressed they-found-no-words-of-Torah clause; it does not restore or alter Hebrew or prove a printing/OCR history. His following he-showed-him pronouns remain without an invented personal antecedent. Both chapter-5 clauses, ויקרא בית ישראל and קראו את שמו מן, are retained separately; the wood and manna interpretations were not newly checked. Hyman’s final numeral is thirty. The whole saved Wikisource Sifrei Bamidbar 160 scalar instead says twenty-three after the three-testimonies argument; both numerals remain distinct, with no silent emendation. The whole saved Davidson Pesachim 54a scalar supports Anah’s disqualified lineage, not a carved idol; its additional genealogy is not imported. A separately selected whole saved Davidson Kiddushin 22b scalar explicitly says Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and kemin chomer, supporting that local identification/title only. The separate Sotah ר״ג remains R-G, with Gamliel only the inherited contextual reading; no full title is transferred and no fresh Sotah witness was read. The earlier Deuteronomy 28:66 parenthesis remains historical explanatory material rather than part of the supplied notice; the Berakhot/Chullin references were not newly checked. Dorshei Chamurot and dorshei reshumot remain interpretive designations, with no personal identity admission. The old HTTP 400/404 Mekhilta ref failures and bounded Sifrei 161 nonmatch remain historical failures/nonmatches, not global absence or retroactive success. All old English, notes and the source hold are retained.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume I, printed p. 327, contains this notice across the columns. It reads אמרו, “said,” where the supplied Wikisource text has אמו; it also explicitly retains thirty in the final sentence. The whole consulted Beeri Mekhilta Vayassa 1 paragraph likewise reads אמרו and interprets the lack of water as words of Torah. Its tree interpretation appears in Beeri’s chapter-1 paragraph 16 and in Silverstein’s following English paragraph; the matching sweat-of-the-brow interpretation is in current Vayassa 5, and the naming of manna is in current Vayassa 6, beside Hyman’s chapters 4 and 5. The whole consulted Sifrei Bamidbar 160 paragraph instead concludes twenty-three; the translation preserves Hyman’s thirty and discloses the difference. Newly consulted Berakhot 24a and Chullin 134b explicitly use Dorshei Chamurot, while Kiddushin 22b explicitly names Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and kemin chomer. Davidson’s English Sotah 15b identifies Rabban Gamliel in the following explanation, while the supplied abbreviation R-G is retained. These are local textual comparisons, not identifications of a single person or group across every occurrence. No extra legal or narrative continuation is inserted into the compressed source. The earlier notes describe the supplied wording and the state before this printed-page and additional passage inspection.
